newsitem.title: UK: Virgin Atlantic lifts air cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Atlantic lifts air cargo rates.

text.p: Virgin Atlantic said on Wednesday it is lifting air cargo rates from the UK by between 3 and 7 percent from April 1, depending on the prevailing market strengths of the routes.
Virgin also listed conditions under which it will drop the temporary fuel surcharge that it introduced on November 4, a Virgin statement said.

The current fuel surcharge will be abolished once the London spot market price for aviation fuel has stabilised at $200 a tonne or less for one month, said Virgin general manager commercial David Woodward.
The Virgin press release said the current spot price is around $210 a tonne, down from a 1997 peak of nearly $300.

As a special concession Virgin said that if the price is at or below $200 on April 1, and if it can anticipate it will not rise, "then the surcharge will be dropped when the (April 1) rate increases are introduced."

"We said from the start that we would remove the surcharge as soon as we could and produced this formula in response to requests from commercial shippers and freight forwarders, who have been asking us for a definite time scale," said Woodward.

"We bore the increase for as long as we could last year, during which time it added nearly 10 million stg to the airline's fuel bill. Since we purchase aviation fuel three months in advance, its price need to stabilise for a month before we can drop the surcharge," said Woodward noting that it was only introduced after fuel prices had dramatically increased in the previous four months to the highest levels for five years.
